subject: Authorization request: SLA concession for AuroraHealth production latency incident
messages:
From: Alex Potter <alex.potter@aurorahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraHealth Contracts <contracts@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 08:50:00 +0200
Subject: Production latency impacting claims ingestion - request for remediation & concession

Irene,

We saw a sustained spike in inference p95 latency starting at ~07:10 UTC this morning that affected our claims ingestion pipeline. For the two-hour window the p95 increased from our usual ~120ms to ~650-800ms and timeouts started cascading into our downstream ETL; several hospitals had delayed claim acknowledgements. Our SLO states 99.9% p95 < 300ms — we're well outside that for an extended period.

This is causing an operational impact for Aurora's billing and we need two things:
- A short summary of root cause and immediate mitigation steps you are taking.
- A proposal for commercial remedy (credit / billing offset) for the impacted window and a commitment that you will mitigate recurrence risk.

We appreciate a prompt timeline — our procurement/legal team will want numbers for the remediation.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Potter
VP, Platform Operations
AuroraHealth

Attachments: (see referenced incident timeline we pulled from observability)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Potter <alex.potter@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:15:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Production latency impacting claims ingestion - request for remediation & concession

Hi Alex — thanks for flagging and very sorry for the disruption. We're pulling the full incident timeline now and have engineers on a live incident bridge. Early findings: a partial capacity misallocation to the eu-west inferencing cluster combined with an atypical sequence-length spike from a customer-side batch caused persistent queueing; autoscaler did not react quickly enough because of a warm-up regression introduced in last week's runtime change.

Immediate actions we have taken (summary):
- Rebalanced live traffic away from the affected GPU pool and routed affected routes to warm standby nodes.
- Manually prefetched KV caches for Aurora's top routes to reduce cold-start overhead.
- Rolled back the autoscaler regression to the prior stable kernel and triggered a controlled scale-up.

I don't want to delay — I'm preparing a concise remedy package and will route for expedited approval. Attached: incident-timeline PDF, draft credit calculation, and an early postmortem outline.

Proposed ask to the leadership team (internal): please advise on the authorization path for a customer-facing concession for a production SLA breach. My initial read: offer a one-month service credit + a capped one-time account credit to offset operational losses as a gesture of goodwill and retention. Alex — can you share the monthly ARR footprint for Aurora so we can calibrate?

Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0132

Attachments: incident-timeline-aurora-2026-07-30.pdf; credit-calculation-aurora.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Authorization request: SLA concession for AuroraHealth production latency incident

Irene — thanks for rapid triage. Two quick things:
1) We need a bounded commercial proposal with fallback options (e.g., percentage credit vs fixed dollar). Finance will push back on uncapped concessions.
2) We must include a mitigation commitment that is measurable (timeline + telemetry threshold) so this doesn't become a recurring ask.

From experience, large health-tech customers expect a mix: an immediate account credit (one-time) plus a short platform-month credit that shows we take reliability seriously. For approval routing: please provide estimated $ value (based on Aurora ARR & expected monthly platform spend) and the exact approval chain (Marissa -> Legal -> CFO).

If you can get me a proposed number within the hour I can pre-approve a discretionary cap so Marissa can finalize sign-off.

Karthik
Head of Sales, EMEA

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, Alex Potter <alex.potter@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Authorization request: SLA concession for AuroraHealth production latency incident

Folks — putting forward a concrete, tiered proposal for approval and public-facing language we can send to Aurora. Numbers are conservative and tied to Aurora's disclosed monthly platform spend (~$200k / month).

Option A (preferred for retention):
- One full month of platform credit (applied to next invoice). Estimated value: $200,000 (applies to usage charges only).
- One-time goodwill account credit of $50,000 to cover integration/operational impact.
- Commitments: formal postmortem delivered within 3 business days; implementation of a pre-warmed standby pool for Aurora routes within 10 business days; quarterly reliability review for next 3 quarters.

Option B (alternative):
- 25% usage credit for the next two billing cycles (~$100k total).
- One-time goodwill credit of $20,000.
- Same mitigation commitments as Option A.

Attachment: credit-calculation-aurora.xlsx (breaks down the math) and postmortem-draft-aurora-2026-07-30.md (early draft).

Alex — please confirm which option you prefer or if legal needs an alternate framing; we'll prepare a DocuSign amendment once approved.

Irene

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Potter <alex.potter@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 12:08:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Authorization request: SLA concession for AuroraHealth production latency incident

Irene / Karthik — reviewed the numbers. Given the clear SLO breach and customer impact in a regulated vertical, I approve Option A (one-month platform credit + $50k one-time credit) conditional on:
- Legal review and a short amendment executed via DocuSign (no change to core SLA language; add remedy schedule).
- A signed mitigation commitment (deliverables + dates) added to the amendment.
- Finance will apply the platform credit to the next invoice and record a one-time revenue adjustment.

Irene, route the amendment to Legal and Finance (cc: me) and paste the DocuSign link when ready. Karthik, thanks for triaging; please loop in CS to coordinate the quarterly reliability reviews.

Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: postmortem-draft-aurora-2026-07-30.md
